sentences.text: Judgment
Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal At the outset, learned counsel for the prays for withdrawal of I.A.No.32329 of 2024, an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
Accordingly, I.A.No.32329 of 2024 is dismissed as withdrawn.
2. With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, this appeal is heard finally.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant after arguing at length on the aspect of commission of penetrative sexual assault as defined in Section 3 of POCSO Act, submits that even if the aspect of penetrative sexual assault is accepted, to be correct then also there are several lacunas in the impugned NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:49700 2 CRA-1606-2024 judgment.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that this appeal under Section 374(2) of Cr.P.C., is filed by the appellant-Premlal, being aggrieved of the judgment dated 25/02/2022, passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Junnardev District Chhindwara (M.P.), in SC No.79/2020, whereby the learned trial Court after recording the evidence against the appellant under Sections 366,
376(2)(i)(k), 506 Part-II of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, 2012, the appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under Premlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185638148/

sentences.text: It is submitted that as per the prosecution story, incident took place on 23/03/2018.
It is pointed out that firstly the Ossification Report (Ex.P/13) is available on record which was proved by Dr. Shikhar Surana (PW-4).

Dr. Shikhar Surana has categorically mentioned that age of the victim was above 16 years and below 17 years, therefore there was no occasion for the learned trial Court to have convicted the appellant under Section 376(2)(i) of IPC, inasmuch as before it was omitted w.e.f.
21/04/2018 it read "(i) commits rape on a woman when she is under 16 years of age;".

6. Thus, when there is a medical evidence is available on record that victim was above 16 years of age, then there was no occasion to invoke the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:49700 3 CRA-1606-2024 provisions of Section 376(2)(i) of IPC.
This shows that learned trial Court Judge was not having proper legal knowledge as to the provision and its application.

7. It is further submitted that despite there being an ossification report available on record, the trial Court considered age of the victim to be 13 years which is contrary to the prosecution case and documents available on record as were filed by the prosecution.

8. It is further submitted that Section 4 of POCSO Act as it stood at the time of the incident, it was provided that 'Whoever commits penetrative sexual assault shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than 7 years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

It is pointed out that this provision was amended w.e.f. 16/08/2019 and it was provided "(2) Whoever commits penetrative sexual assault on a child below 16 years of age shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than 20 years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of natural life of that person, and shall also be liable to fine.
9.

It is also submitted that this amended provision came into effect w.e.f. 16/08/2019 whereas offence is of the year 2018 and therefore, punishment will be as per the unamended provision, and this basic fact was ignored, over looked and grossly neglected by the learned trial Court Judge while handing over the punishment.

Thus, it is submitted that the trial Court Judge was not well versed in legal provisions and also on the aspect that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:49700 4 Premlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185638148/
2 CRA-1606-2024 punishment was required to be handed over as was provided under the unamended provision which stood as on the date of commission of the offence and not of the subsequent dates.
10.

sentences.text: It is also pointed out that the FSL report though available on record at page 37 dated 19/04/2018 bearing No.BI/475/2018 issued by the Assistant Chemical Examiner, State of M.P. Regional Forensic Science Laboratory, Bhopal and addressed to Superintended of Police, Chhindwara, is available on record, but neither it was exhibited nor any question was put to the accused under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. despite the fact that learned trial Court has used that report in Para-24 of the impugned judgment.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Thus, it is pointed out that the learned trial Court was totally oblivious of appreciation of legal provisions, understanding of law and also its application.

11. Shri Manas Mani Verma, learned Government Advocate submits that even otherwise when Section 4 of POCSO Act remains unamended, if put to use prescribed life imprisonment, therefore sentence of 20 years cannot be faulted with.
12. We are in total disagreement with the contention put-forth by Shri Manas Mani Verma, learned Public Prosecutor.
The Senior Additional District Judge is suppose to understand law and apply it in its full force.

We do not expect a Senior Additional District Judge given responsibility of acting as a Special Judge to be oblivious of legal provisions and understanding of the concerned Judge calls for a detailed scrutiny and investigation for which, we direct this file to be placed before Hon'ble the Chief Justice to take a call and decide as to whether the concerned Judge is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:49700 5 CRA-1606-2024 required to undergo refresher course or is entitled to continue in service as a Special Judge.
13. As far as merits are concerned, we are of the opinion that prosecution has proved the commission of offence.
Therefore, without dwelling on the aspect of conviction, we would like to record two findings, namely; conviction under Section 376(2)(i) of IPC is not made out and is hereby set aside.

Secondly, the finding of the learned trial Court recorded in Para-38 that the age of the victim was 13 years, is not made out as contrary to the Ossification Report (Ex.P/13) of Expert which is proved by Dr. Shikhar Surana (PW-4), who categorically proved the age of the victim to be more than 16 years.

Therefore, under such facts and circumstances, while maintaining conviction under Sections 366, 506 Part-II of IPC r/w Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, we hold that appellant will undergo sentence of 10 years R.I. under Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, as it stood prior to the date of amendment i.e. 16/08/2019.
Other sentences shall remain intact.
All the sentences to run concurrently.
14. In above temrs, the appeal is partly allowed and disposed of.
